paper_metadata.title: Enhancing Domain-Independent Knowledge Graph Construction through OpenIE Cleaning and LLMs Validation
paper_metadata.venue: Procedia Computer Science; 28th International Conference on Knowledge-Based and Intelligent Information & Engineering Systems (KES 2024)
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper proposes G-T2KG, a domain-independent knowledge-graph construction pipeline that combines OpenIE with noun-phrase-based cleaning and LLM-based validation. The method aims to reduce incorrect triplets while preserving recall without domain-specific adaptations. It is evaluated on computer-science and music gold standards constructed by the authors. Results show higher recall than selected state-of-the-art approaches on the computer-science corpus, improved precision after LLM validation, and satisfactory performance on the music corpus.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses automatic construction of knowledge graphs from raw, unstructured text when domain-specific NER and relation-extraction systems improve precision but reduce domain independence, while OpenIE preserves broad coverage but produces many incorrect triplets. The objective is to build a reusable, domain-independent pipeline that cleans OpenIE outputs and validates extracted triplets against their source sentences using an LLM.

methodology.description: G-T2KG processes raw text through five sequential components. C1 performs corpus cleaning, coreference resolution, and sentence segmentation. C2 extracts triplets with OpenIE6 and extracts hypernym or is-a relations with a pattern-based Hypernym Relation Extractor. C3 cleans OpenIE triplets using predicate rectification, stopword removal, lemmatization, noun-phrase checks, and either Stanford CoreNLP dependency-tree analysis (Option 1) or zero-shot GPT-4 head identification (Option 2). Cleaned OpenIE triplets are merged with hypernym triplets. C4 validates each triplet by converting it into an affirmation and asking GPT-4 whether it corresponds to the source sentence; invalid triplets are filtered. C5 maps entities and predicates using the approach adopted from SciCero to reduce label heterogeneity. Mapping is deliberately performed after validation so that mapped labels not present in the sentence do not complicate verification. The architecture is therefore a modular hybrid of symbolic/syntactic processing, neural OpenIE, pattern-based extraction, zero-shot LLM cleaning/validation, and post-extraction mapping. The paper does not report entity typing as part of the implemented pipeline.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The proposed method is domain-independent and does not require a fixed domain ontology or schema for extraction. It produces open subject-predicate-object triplets. Predicate mapping is used later to reduce heterogeneity, and hypernym-pattern extraction adds is-a relations. The evaluation uses manually constructed gold standards rather than an ontology-driven target schema.

text_to_kg_stages: Text preprocessing: corpus cleaning, coreference resolution, and sentence segmentation
Entity and concept extraction: noun-phrase identification and cleaning of subject/object arguments
Relation and triple extraction: OpenIE6 and pattern-based hypernym extraction
Knowledge fusion and deduplication: merging cleaned OpenIE triplets with hypernym triplets and mapping entities/predicates
Graph validation and correction: GPT-4 source-sentence validation and filtering
Graph construction: formation of a knowledge graph from validated and mapped triplets

input_output.input_granularity: Sentence-level extraction evaluated within document/abstract-level corpora
input_output.output_representation: Validated subject-predicate-object triplets, including hypernym/is-a relations, subsequently mapped at the entity and predicate level to reduce label heterogeneity and form a knowledge graph

models_and_tools: Deep neural-network-based OpenIE with coordination analysis
Pattern-based Hypernym Relation Extractor using predefined patterns
GPT-4 for zero-shot noun-phrase head identification in Option 2
Entity and predicate mapping approach adopted from SciCero
GPT-4 few-shot baselines with four examples and an instruction-refined experiment
datasets: CS-GS: 12 computer-science abstracts from the Web of Science dataset, 108 sentences, 180 gold triplets, 247 unique entities, and 100 unique predicates
Music GS: one randomly selected document titled '20th Century Music' from the referenced music corpus, 100 sentences, 410 gold triplets, 488 unique entities, and 155 unique predicates

baselines: GPT-4-Exp 1: few-shot prompting with four examples and paragraph context
GPT-4-Exp 2: instruction-refined GPT-4 extraction addressing coreference, pronouns, conjunctions, and mentions
evaluation.setting: Three annotators manually matched extracted triplets to gold-standard triplets using majority vote. Correct triplets absent from the gold standard were added during evaluation. The computer-science corpus compared G-T2KG variants with SciCero and two GPT-4 extraction experiments; the music corpus evaluated G-T2KG variants only. Results were reported separately for the Stanford CoreNLP dependency-tree cleaning option and the GPT-4 head-identification option, each with and without GPT-4 triplet validation.

value: On the computer-science corpus, G-T2KG Option 1 with validation achieved 72.07% precision, 44.44% recall, and 54.98% F1; without validation it achieved 58.50% precision, 47.77% recall, and 52.59% F1.
On the computer-science corpus, G-T2KG Option 2 with validation achieved 75.00% precision, 41.66% recall, and 53.56% F1; without validation it achieved 50.00% precision, 44.44% recall, and 47.05% F1.

SciCero achieved 72.09% precision, 17.22% recall, and 27.50% F1 on the computer-science corpus. GPT-4-Exp 1 achieved 25.65% precision, 32.77% recall, and 28.77% F1; GPT-4-Exp 2 achieved 27.81% precision, 43.88% recall, and 34.04% F1.
On the music corpus, G-T2KG Option 1 with validation achieved 64.88% precision, 35.12% recall, and 45.57% F1; Option 2 with validation achieved 63.97% precision, 36.60% recall, and 46.56% F1.
The authors report that GPT-4 validation increased precision by 14% to 25% while reducing recall by up to 3.3%, depending on the configuration and corpus.

The authors report that G-T2KG outperformed SciCero in recall on the computer-science corpus and that G-T2KG identified triplets missed by SciCero. These are authors' interpretations of the reported experiments, not cross-dataset generalizations.

value: Combines broad-coverage OpenIE extraction with syntactic cleaning and LLM validation while retaining a domain-independent design.
The pipeline includes coordination analysis through OpenIE6 and a separate hypernym extractor intended to reduce information loss and enrich is-a relations.
GPT-4 validation substantially improves precision in the reported ablations while causing only a limited recall reduction.
The method is evaluated on two distinct domains and the paper provides newly constructed gold standards.
The authors report public release of source code and the developed gold standards.

value: The sequential pipeline can propagate errors from one component into later components, producing cumulative inaccuracies.
Multiple separate deep-learning-based models may increase execution time and resource requirements for large corpora.
Using GPT-4 for validation is unsuitable for confidential medical or economic data because source text must be sent to the external model.
GPT-4 validation improves precision at the cost of some recall.
The music-domain evaluation does not compare G-T2KG against other methods.

Confidential-data deployment remains unresolved while validation depends on an external GPT-4 service.
Entity typing is not yet incorporated into the proposed pipeline and is identified as future work.
The absence of universal ontology-independent gold standards remains an evaluation challenge.
The paper does not establish how well the approach scales to large corpora or how its runtime and resource costs compare with alternatives.
